en.html:
The Mandokoro's public officers were sent together to the diagonal-front audience seats. A pillar obstructed the view. Worst place for enjoying Noh; exactly the right place for our rank.

We had permission to watch the performance. The pillar had permission to prevent it. Both arrangements could now be honored without inconveniencing anybody important. For the next several hours, perhaps I would become a considerable authority on this particular piece of wood. Grain, proportion, refusal to move. Wah. A very consistent performer.

The senior officials, for whom all this was principally arranged, had not arrived yet. But a large man who appeared to be Doushin Yusa was already present. Such readiness from such a high position. Perhaps the host was making an effort.

The Kubo's stylish hitatare was nothing new. Today there was a navy hood also. What was the idea behind that addition?

en.html:
The officials and their families had taken their places, but the central seat at the front remained empty. Who belonged there, that was understood.

Soon an imposing party appeared. Most of the imposing was being done by the ladies-in-waiting and guards surrounding its head. They made for the chief guest's seat.

Shirou Kuniuji Ashikaga.

The boy would inherit his dead grandfather's position as Lord General of the Six Guards. Head of Rokuhara—no, of the entire realm.

He walked quietly. Not looking particularly happy with the arrangement. Then, all at once, he turned his head. As though one gaze among all the others had felt different.

In that direction—Sakurako Okabe.

His eyes widened. Like everybody else, he had probably not expected her here.

He blinked, checked again. Then the surprise became a happiness he could not keep down.

He had seen the small ornament in her hair. One of the flowers he had sent.

Princess Sakurako answered his look with a little smile.

So many people between them. Still, the invisible thread had connected.

Princess Sakurako answered his look with a little smile.

So many people between them. Still, the invisible thread had connected.

ja.html:
一通り高官やその妻子らが座に着いた後も、正面の
中央、主賓の席はまだ空いたままだった。
　誰がそこへ着くのかはわかっている。

　程なく。
　一際物々しい集団――それは集団の頭たる人物より
周りを固める女官や警護兵によるところが大きかった
――が現れて、その主賓席へ向かう。

　足利四郎邦氏である。
　やがて六衛大将領の地位を死せる祖父から受け継ぎ、
六波羅の……否、天下の棟梁となるべき少年。

　さして心楽しくもなさそうに静々と歩く彼は、ふと、
唐突に顔の向きを変えた。
　何か、種類の異なる視線を感じ取ったかのように。

　一方向を見る。
　……岡部桜子。

　少年の眼が驚きに見開かれた。
　誰もがそうであろうが、この会でその姿を見るとは
思わなかったのだろう。

　確認する風で瞼を瞬かせ、改めて見直す。
　そして、驚きの表情は抑え難い喜びに変じた。

　姫の容姿を彩る、ささやかな装飾を見て取ったのだ。
　彼が贈り届けた花――その一輪。

　少年の眼差しに、桜子姫が小さく笑みを返す。
　
　人垣を隔てて、見えざる糸が確かに繋がった。

en.html:
Noh expertise I did not possess. Even so, this performer's skill was plain to me.

Every movement had stature. Every sweep of the fan carried a warrior's force.

And the voice, above all. A good singing voice was one thing. This was another level altogether.

Feeling.

The art was there in the rise and fall of his words. But inside the art, something raw was living.

A warrior doomed to defeat. His sorrow, sung in a melody of extraordinary beauty...

Dono saath. Both together. The throat did not say, first I will sing beautifully, afterward kindly imagine the suffering. Beauty came out, and the hurt was already inside it. No separating them now. A man could not even admire the skill in peace.

That was the rare thing. A master's work, surely.

From what I could see, perhaps the Zaou school of the Kongou line...

The second half of Yorimasa chiefly showed the battle as he told it. Very little explanation of the man's inner life. The very thing that makes a tragedy hurt, it did not spend many words on.

Still, somehow, it was reaching us.

Why this man, Yorimasa Minamoto, had to fight. What was in his heart as he fought.

That anguish.

That grief.

A hand moved, a foot moved, and a whole human life was there.

—I could see him.

A man with the wings of a tsurugi, who could fly, and still chose to enter the river with his soldiers. Such daring, lifting the courage of his side.

The Noh stage is not a stage. It is a world.

People say that. With an actor of sufficient power, the saying becomes a plain statement of fact.

Now another world stood before us.

The Uji River, seven hundred and sixty years ago.

—Or Inawashiro in Aizu, only last month.

　その中には何より頼りとした肉親もいる。

　老将はもはや一人。

On the grass, he spread his fan.

He threw off his armor, sat down, and drew his sword.

Then he sang his death poem, one last verse.

ja.html:
芝の上に、扇を敷き。
　鎧を脱ぎ捨てて座り、刀を抜く。

　そうして、歌う――
　辞世の一句を。

芝の上に、扇を敷き。

　そうして、歌う――
　辞世の一句を。

en.html:
《This buried tree never bloomed with flowers,
and how pitiful, the end my body has come to.》

　身のなる果ては哀れなりけり》

en.html:
—He had known it would never flower.

Still he had to rise. Still it had to end like this. For himself, what was left except pity?
en.text:
—He had known it would never flower.

Still he had to rise. Still it had to end like this. For himself, what was left except pity?

――花が咲かぬ事はわかっていた。
　それでも立ち上がり、こうして果てるほかなかった
己を哀れむばかりだ。

en.html: Sakurako"...Father...!"

ja.html: 桜子「……父上っ……！」

en.html:
Yorimasa left.

The traveling monk's dream came to an end.

The performance closed quietly. To the last, quietly...

Only the daughter's low sobs disturbed the air of the Noh hall. Her father was gone.
